title: Lands End Coastal Trail
content: San Francisco's classic coastal walk: 3.4 miles round trip past the Sutro Baths ruins, cypress groves, and nonstop Golden Gate views. Mostly flat with a few staircases; doable in sneakers. Start at the Lands End Lookout parking lot. Often foggy in summer mornings - clearest in fall.

title: Batteries to Bluffs Trail
content: Short but dramatic 2.2-mile out-and-back along the Presidio's wild western bluffs, connecting historic gun batteries with a staircase descent to hidden Marshall's Beach. The best close-up Golden Gate Bridge photos in the city. Reachable by Muni; combine with Crissy Field for a longer day.

title: Mount Sutro Loop
content: A 2.5-mile forest loop through eucalyptus cloud forest in the middle of the city - on foggy days the canopy drips and it feels like another planet. Soft dirt trails, gentle grades, entrances near UCSF Parnassus. The city's best secret lunch-break hike.

title: Angel Island Perimeter Loop
content: Ferry from the Embarcadero, then a 5.5-mile paved-and-dirt loop around the island with 360-degree bay views: city skyline, both bridges, Marin headlands. Add the Mount Livermore summit spur (+1.5 miles, 788 ft) for the full panorama. Bring lunch; the ferry schedule sets your pace.

title: Marin Headlands: Rodeo Beach to Hill 88
content: A 5.2-mile loop from Rodeo Beach up past Battery Townsley to the abandoned radar station on Hill 88, returning via the Coastal Trail. About 1,000 ft of climbing, huge Pacific views, and Cold War ruins to explore. Exposed and windy - bring a shell even when the city is warm.

title: Tennessee Valley to Tennessee Beach
content: The Bay Area's easiest reward-to-effort ratio: a flat 3.4-mile round trip down a green valley to a black-sand cove beach. Family-friendly, stroller-passable to the last stretch. Parking lot fills by 10am on weekends - go early. No dogs allowed.

title: Dipsea Trail: Mill Valley to Stinson Beach
content: The famous one: 7.4 miles point-to-point over the shoulder of Mount Tamalpais, starting with the 688 Dipsea stairs and ending with your feet in the sand at Stinson. Around 2,200 ft of total climbing through redwoods, chaparral, and coastal ridges. Take the Marin Transit bus back, or arrange a shuttle.

title: Steep Ravine to Pantoll Loop
content: A 4.6-mile Mount Tam loop climbing Steep Ravine's fern canyon - complete with a wooden ladder beside a waterfall - then returning on the Matt Davis trail with ocean views. Around 1,100 ft of gain. Best in winter and spring when the creek runs full. Trailhead at Stinson Beach.

title: Muir Woods Canopy View Loop
content: Skip the stroller crowds on the valley floor: this 4-mile loop climbs the Canopy View Trail through old-growth redwoods to Fern Creek, quiet within ten minutes of the entrance. About 800 ft of gain. Parking requires a reservation - book weeks ahead or take the shuttle from Sausalito.

title: Mount Tamalpais East Peak via Verna Dunshee
content: Drive or ride to the East Peak lot, then a 0.7-mile paved loop around the summit plus a short scramble to the fire lookout at 2,571 ft. On clear days you can see the Sierra; on foggy days you float above a white ocean. The biggest view-per-step in the Bay Area.

title: Sweeney Ridge from Skyline College
content: A 4.8-mile round trip on the ridge where the Portolá expedition first sighted San Francisco Bay in 1769. Paved and dirt path, ~600 ft of gain, with the bay on one side and the Pacific on the other. Frequently socked in - check the fog forecast; it makes or breaks this one.

title: Montara Mountain from Gray Whale Cove
content: A 7-mile round trip climbing from Highway 1 to Montara Mountain's 1,898-ft summit, with whale-watching potential in winter and spring wildflowers. Steady 1,800 ft of climbing on fire roads and singletrack. One of the Peninsula coast's toughest regular workouts.

title: Purisima Creek Redwoods Loop
content: A 7.4-mile loop in the Santa Cruz Mountains above Half Moon Bay: descend through second-growth redwoods along Purisima Creek, climb back on Harkins Ridge with ocean glimpses. About 1,600 ft of gain, shaded and cool even in summer heat. Weekday solitude is nearly guaranteed.

title: Mission Peak at Sunrise
content: The Bay Area's rite of passage: 6 miles round trip, 2,100 ft of relentless open-grassland climbing to the famous summit pole above Fremont. Start before dawn for sunrise over the whole bay and to beat the heat - there is zero shade. Bring double the water you think you need.

title: Redwood Regional Park: Stream Trail Loop
content: Oakland's surprise: a 4.5-mile loop through a genuine redwood canyon fifteen minutes from downtown. Gentle grades along the creek with ladybug swarms in late fall. Combine Stream, French, and Orchard trails; picnic areas at both ends. Dogs welcome on most trails.

title: Berkeley Fire Trails via Strawberry Canyon
content: The East Bay's favorite training run: a 4-mile out-and-back on wide fire roads above the UC Berkeley campus, ~900 ft of gain, with Golden Gate views framed by eucalyptus. Walkable from campus and the Clark Kerr neighborhood. Muddy but magical after winter rain.
